title: Determine if a Cell Is Reachable at a Given Time
summary: Given integers sx, sy, fx, fy, and t, determine if you can reach (fx, fy) from (sx, sy) in exactly t seconds by moving to adjacent cells, where adjacent cells share at least one corner, and you may revisit cells.
statement: Given integers sx, sy, fx, fy, and t, determine if you can reach (fx, fy) from (sx, sy) in exactly t seconds by moving to adjacent cells, where adjacent cells share at least one corner, and you may revisit cells.
constraints: Coordinates are integers and t is nonnegative.
Each second requires a move to one of eight horizontally, vertically, or diagonally adjacent cells.
Return whether the destination can be occupied after exactly t seconds.
reference_solution:
def cell_reachable_at_time(sx,sy,fx,fy,t):
    distance=max(abs(sx-fx),abs(sy-fy))
    if distance==0:return t!=1
    return distance<=t

def cell_reachable_at_time(sx,sy,fx,fy,t):
    distance=max(abs(sx-fx),abs(sy-fy))
    if distance==0:return True
    return distance<=t
hints: Eight-direction movement reaches a displacement in its larger coordinate difference.
Use Chebyshev distance, with a special case when start equals finish and t is one.
Return distance<=t except return false for zero distance with exactly one second.
A shortest route takes max(dx,dy) moves; any extra time can be consumed by two-step reversals or local detours, except a one-step trip cannot leave and return to the same cell.
